articles.title: Iran's guards claim incidents involving seven ships near Hormuz
articles.dek: Four vessels were allegedly struck and three hit mines; ship identities are not independently confirmed.
articles.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy claimed four ships involved in oil transfers were struck in the Gulf and three more hit mines west of Hormuz.
body: The strait is essential to world energy shipping. Iran's statement did not identify ships, flags or crews or provide independent damage assessments.

These are Tehran's claims, not seven independently established losses. Verified maritime evidence is needed to assess the damage.

articles.title: Putin signals possible talks as Donbas dispute remains unresolved
articles.dek: The Kremlin seeks a security framework for Russia, Ukraine and Europe, but no agreement has been signed.
articles.summary: Russia's president said on 22 October that negotiations should address a postwar security system and entertained renewed US-mediated contacts.

Russia emphasizes territory and security, while Ukraine demands sovereignty, a ceasefire and guarantees. Attribution does not make territorial invasion legally equivalent to national self-defence.

articles.title: Gaza food assistance shrinks for roughly half a million people
articles.dek: WFP reduces monthly beneficiaries from 1.6 million to 1.1 million.
articles.summary: On 22 October the World Food Programme's cuts, announced on 19 October, were taking effect, leaving an estimated half-million fewer people receiving monthly assistance.
